text.p: The Turkish lira weakened to 88,450 per dollar from 87,940 at Monday's close due to a higher dollar/mark parity and the central bank's dollar rate for banks' compulsory hard currency transfers set at 88,275 lira.
Overnight money rates traded between 67-74.5 percent during the day and closed at 69 percent. The average rate was 74.35 percent on Monday.

The treasury sold 106.9 trillion lira worth of March 12, 1997 paper, meeting 56 percent of total bids worth 192.1 trillion lira. It raised the average yield to 128.92 percent from 117.50 percent at the previous 112-day t-bill auction on September 3.

A cash shortage is expected on Wednesday when banks will cash in 57.7 trillion lira from the treasury for maturing t-bills and from the central bank for maturing reverse repo. They will pay the treasury 69.6 trillion lira for the auction.
The central bank said it would open a five-day repo auction tomorrow to feed cash to the system.
Yields eased on t-bills maturing in 1996 but firmed on 1997 maturity papers.

The yield on the most heavily traded December 25 paper dived to 113.90 percent from an average of 115 percent on Monday. The second active February 12 paper yielded 127.67 percent, up from yesterday's 127.50 percent.
March 12 papers, sold in today's auction, also traded lower at 126.17 percent with Wednesday's value date after the auction. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
